title: FIFPRO Include Some Surprises in World XI Nominees for 2026
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Grey Whitebloom11:45 AM ESTLionel Messi (left) and Lamine Yamal represent the past, present and future of this award. / Luis ROBAYO/AFP/Getty Images (Messi), David Ramirez/Soccrates/Getty Images (Yamal)Almost two decades after they were first recognized by their peers, Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo have once again been nominated for the FIFPRO World XI, joining the modern gems of Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé in the running.

This prestigious honor calls upon the opinion of licensed professionals, with more than 26,000 members of FIFPRO, effectively a trade union for soccer players, voting on the best goalkeeper, defender, midfielder and forward of the 2025–26 season. Unlike the Ballon d’Or, which is decided by journalists, FIFPRO’s World XI takes pride in being “the only global football award decided exclusively by professional footballers.”
Fans will have to wait until Monday, Nov. 9 for the final XI to be unveiled, but the 26 male and female players with the most votes have been revealed to form the two rosters under consideration.

As many as 19,806 players from 73 countries cast their vote for the three best goalkeepers, defenders, midfielders and forwards. The final roll call closely mirrors the 30-man Ballon d’Or shortlist which recently ended with Harry Kane as the winner. However, there are some notable discrepancies.

The most eye-catching is the presence of Ronaldo. The veteran forward hasn’t been nominated for the Ballon d’Or since 2022 and is currently arguing over his goal tally in the Saudi Pro League but managed to secure a spot in this ranking chosen exclusively by other players. By contrast Fabián Ruiz, who won the Champions League and World Cup to finish 10th in the Ballon d’Or, did not even get nominated.
Alexia Putellas was born to reign. pic.twitter.com/NlzNmcTJei

There are more differences between the women’s Ballon d’Or shortlist and FIFPRO’s roster of nominees. Barcelona typically dominated both after winning every available trophy while losing just one game, but there was also room for some legendary figures entering the later days of their career. Lucy Bronze, for instance, got the nod despite appearing in barely more than half of Chelsea’s league fixtures.
